thread.title: Sell This 8% Junk And Buy The 7.22% With Massive Upside Potential

author: Colorado Wealth Management Fund
title: Sell This 8% Junk And Buy The 7.22% With Massive Upside Potential
text:
This research report was produced by The REIT Forum with assistance from Big Dog Investments .
Every investment isn’t going to make you money.
Sometimes we must sell the junk yields.
And buy the great ones.
While I like preferred shares for their relatively low risk and high yields, some of them are not worth investing in. Why invest in an 8% yield with substantial call risk and no upside when you can invest in a 7% REIT with excellent upside potential?
Let’s begin.
Preferred share For investors interested in The REIT Forum’s preferred share ratings, see my guide to preferred shares . I also have a guide for preferred share dividend captures .
AG Mortgage Investment Trust’s ( MITT ) preferred shares, especially the A series, have too much call risk.
Source: CWMF’s subscriber spreadsheet (subscription required for 50+ preferred shares and baby bonds with comparing prices)
MITT may be able to issue new shares with a coupon rate around 7.5%. They would save 75 basis points by calling the A shares and 50 basis points by calling the B shares. At the very least, calling the A shares for a 75 basis point savings would make sense. Issuing a new preferred share can often cost and $0.75 per share in issuance cost. They would recover that in about 4 years on the A series and 6 years on the B series. Note 75 basis points is 0.75%. It is also $0.1875.
As you can see above, there is no more call protection on the calendar except for the 30-day notice companies will give on a call.
I believe the risks on MITT’s preferred shares make them unsuitable for the buy-and-hold investor. Further, at recent prices, these securities are not attractively priced for traders.
Brixmor Property Group Brixmor Property Group ( BRX ) is a strip center REIT.
Source: BRX investor presentation
The strip center REITs have a great deal in common with mall REITs, but the anchor properties are often grocery stores. BRX may prove viable for trading, but the real strength lies in the buy-and-hold proposition. This is a severely discounted REIT with a very solid business model. They have a solid track record of dividend growth, a pretty large yield, plenty of AFFO coverage, and room for AFFO to continue growing as they roll over expiring leases. I’m giving BRX a buy rating and own a position.
Investors need to understand the way ABR PSF growth is calculated.
Source: BRX investor presentation
Each REIT scores their ABR PSF across the entire portfolio and has a year-end number (they also do this quarterly) to show the change in ABR PSF. If a REIT sells off all their lowest rent properties, their ABR PSF will increase rapidly. This metric does not adjust for “same property”.
We want to look at the results BRX has in their leasing activity (left side of slide above). This should give us a better idea of how they are doing at growing revenues for comparable spaces.
The new leasing spreads for BRX are downright excellent. They are a leader in growing their leasing rates. In the second part of the image, we can see that 4.3% of the portfolio ABR comes from new leases the company signed. Because BRX is one of the largest strip-center REITs, they also lead in sheer dollar terms of new total dollars in ABR.
The important metric isn’t where ABR was in prior years, it is where ABR will be in the next several years. The improvements in leasing rates demonstrate substantial growth:
Source: BRX investor presentation
BRX began with very low numbers for ABR, but they have been very successful at raising the rates on new leases. Where most REITs are concerned about current leases expiring, a substantial portion of ABR’s property is under contract at rates at are below market rates. That makes it easier for management to raise rates on the renewals. Some tenants will leave, but they will rarely find a better deal elsewhere.
Full analysis on Brixmor Property Group (subscription to The REIT Forum required)
McDonald’s McDonald’s ( MCD ) is a sin stock. Just like big tobacco’s large players Philip Morris ( PM ) and Altria Group ( MO ), McDonald’s will kill you.
Obesity challenges tobacco use as a leading cause of preventable death.
Photo source
The stock has soared and surpassed all of my expectations. They have another potential tailwind. Since private equity bought out Panera a while back, they have run the company poorly. Panera has been shrinking serving sizes, encouraging customers to tip, and cutting back on checking order accuracy. In a nutshell, they are doing less of the activities that allowed them to decimate their peers.
The success for McDonald’s was driven by a couple factors. The biggest factor may have been their decision to continue serving terrible food at a faster rate. I did not believe this would be an incredible success. I was under the impression that McDonald’s would need to improve the quality of their food.
I was wrong.
They reduced their options on the menu and it allowed them to improve drive-thru times.
They are now able to serve more artery-clogging “food” each hour. The surprise for me is McDonald’s high share price when the other dividends champions are out of favor. Walmart ( WMT ) is still suffering from analysts ditching them after their online growth slowed. Today, online growth is the major metric that analysts care about.
The tech sector is hot. Investors are focused on performance from Microsoft ( MSFT ), Apple ( AAPL ), Facebook ( FB ), Google ( GOOG ), Amazon ( AMZN ), and Netflix ( NFLX ). These tech companies have been driving the returns for the total market. The dividend champions are simply ignored as investors find them to be dull. I disagree. Consumer staples and utilities are excellent sectors for finding dividend champions. They often have lower volatility to go with the higher yield. Because of the low volatility and high yield, they are often suitable stocks for retirees and other income-oriented investors. The best area to find these yields is REITs.
There are several great REITs at very attractive prices. For instance, Simon Property Group ( SPG ) and AvalonBay ( AVB ) both have A- rated balance sheets and solid earnings growth year after year. They offer investors a high dividend yield and both REITs excel at maximizing the value of their assets. Simon Property Group owns, operates, and redevelops high-quality malls. AvalonBay owns apartment buildings in gateway markets. In addition to owning and operating the apartments, they also develop new apartment buildings at attractive yields. Their expertise in development adds additional value for shareholders.
